newsitem.title: USA: Bond rating groups laud DC panel's strategic plan.
newsitem.headline: Bond rating groups laud DC panel's strategic plan.

text.p: Bond rating agencies on Friday lauded a plan issued by the District of Columbia financial control board as a pivotal step toward revitalizing a struggling D.C.

The 46-page "strategic plan" released Thursday warns that the District cannot emerge from financial crisis unless the U.S. government assumes financing of up to $1 billion in city programs, including Medicaid, mental health care, prisons and infrastructure.
"This is really the first step toward addressing the fundamental" structural problems of the District, Barbara Flickinger, vice president for Moody's Investors Service, said in a telephone interview.
"At a minimum, it's going to start the debate, which is healthy," Flickinger said.
Richard Raphael, executive managing director for Fitch Investors Service, called the report a "good ... balanced" step.

"The control board is looking at how D.C. can do things better, but at the same time stating clearly that there is a federal role," Raphael said in a telephone interview. He said because the control board has "credibility" with Congress, its recommendation will get close scrutiny.
Parry Young, director of public finance for Standard & Poor's Ratings Group, on Thursday called the board's report "encouraging."
"A lot of the issues (addressed in the report) are issues we've talked about for years," Young said in a telephone interview.
"But the fact that the board has established timetables and plans for dealing with these problems is encouraging," Young said.

The control board report sets out a detailed timetable for tackling the city's problems. By March 31, for instance, the board will recommend key structural changes in city financing, including detailed proposals on services that should be handed over to the federal government.
